allow_large: The owner allowed it on 2026-10-01: a new roadmap command, so the command table and existing command tests change with it
done_when: forge roadmap retire <key> --by <spec> marks a pending roadmap item superseded and records the spec that replaces it, in a fix like other roadmap changes; it refuses with a plain message for an unknown key, an item already started or done, or a spec that doesn't exist; forge next and the board stop listing superseded items, and the roadmap merge rule keeps the superseded status. The skill's intent table has a row for it. Command-level tests cover retiring a pending item, each refusal, and next no longer listing it.

findings.body: A concurrent story start can undo the listing suppression: retire a pending item in a fix, then start its story from main before the retirement lands. `story.new` checks only roadmap membership (src/forge/story.py:124–129), so this succeeds. Once the retirement lands, this filter removes the key from `titles`, but the fallback at src/forge/board.py:112 adds it back from `found` and displays the story. `forge next` likewise processes the surviving story state without checking superseded status (src/forge/nextstep.py:153–160). Exclude superseded keys from these state-derived listings too. This concerns the concurrent-start edge case; it does not dispute the coordinator's merge-ranking ruling.
findings.title: Exclude superseded keys from state-derived listings

why: Roadmap items a new spec replaces can only be deleted by hand from plans/roadmap.json, because Forge has no command for it and no status for a replaced item
